title: Mass Uprising Ousts General Ershad
description: Following months of escalating protests led by the Awami League, BNP, and student groups, General H.M. Ershad resigned on 6 December 1990 after eight years of military-backed rule. Chief Justice Shahabuddin Ahmed assumed power as acting president to oversee a transition to democracy, ending Bangladesh's second era of authoritarian rule.

title: BNP Victory and First Female Prime Minister
description: The general election on 27 February 1991 — widely regarded as free and fair — brought Khaleda Zia's BNP to power with 140 seats. Zia was sworn in as Bangladesh's first female prime minister, beginning competitive two-party democracy after years of military rule.

title: Devastating Cyclone Kills 138,000
description: On 29 April 1991 a Category-5 equivalent cyclone (260 km/h winds) made landfall south of Chittagong, generating a 6-metre storm surge. Approximately 138,000 people were killed, 10 million left homeless, and US$1.7 billion in damage recorded. The catastrophe prompted significant international aid and accelerated investment in coastal cyclone shelters.

title: Twelfth Constitutional Amendment Restores Parliamentary System
description: In September 1991 a referendum approved the Twelfth Amendment to the constitution by 84% in favour, restoring Westminster-style parliamentary government and transferring executive power from the president to the prime minister. The reform reversed the presidentialization imposed by the Fourth Amendment of 1975.

title: Opposition Hartal Campaign and Parliamentary Boycott
description: From late 1993 into 1994 the Awami League, Jatiyo Party, and Jamaat-e-Islami launched a sustained general-strike (hartal) campaign accusing the BNP government of corruption and electoral fraud in the 1993 Mirpur by-election. All three parties formally boycotted parliament in early 1994, paralyzing legislative business and triggering prolonged political confrontation.

title: Magura By-Election Rigging Allegations
description: Widespread allegations of rigging in the March 1994 Magura parliamentary by-election hardened the opposition's position that elections could not be held fairly under a sitting government. The scandal accelerated demands for a neutral caretaker government system that would eventually be institutionalized in 1996.

title: Thirteenth Amendment Enshrines Caretaker Government System
description: Following a boycotted February 1996 poll that returned the BNP unopposed, parliament passed the Thirteenth Amendment in March 1996 mandating that all future elections be held under a neutral non-partisan caretaker government. The reform became the constitutional cornerstone of Bangladesh's transitional democracy for the next 15 years.

title: Awami League Wins Election; Sheikh Hasina Becomes Prime Minister
description: In the June 1996 general election, the first under the new caretaker system, the Awami League won 146 seats and Sheikh Hasina was sworn in as prime minister — the first time the party had governed since 1975. Her first term oversaw improved India relations and an economic opening.

title: Ganges Water-Sharing Treaty with India
description: On 12 December 1996 Bangladesh and India signed a 30-year water-sharing treaty governing flows at the Farakka Barrage, ending decades of dispute over the Ganges. The agreement guaranteed Bangladesh at least 35,000 cusecs in alternate 10-day cycles during the critical dry season months of March–May.

title: Chittagong Hill Tracts Peace Accord
description: On 2 December 1997 the Hasina government and the Parbatya Chattagram Jana Sanghati Samiti (PCJSS) signed the Chittagong Hill Tracts Peace Accord, ending a two-decade insurgency that had killed thousands. The accord granted limited autonomy to the indigenous communities of the hill tracts, though full implementation remained contested.

title: Catastrophic Floods Submerge Two-Thirds of the Country
description: From July to September 1998 Bangladesh experienced its worst floods in recorded history: over 75% of the country was inundated, including half of Dhaka. Around 30 million people were rendered homeless, more than 1,000 died, 700,000 hectares of crops were destroyed, and 400 factories were forced to close, causing an estimated 20% drop in economic output.

title: Export Processing Zone Expansion and RMG Growth
description: By the late 1990s Bangladesh's ready-made garment (RMG) sector had become the dominant export earner, employing over two million workers — predominantly women — and generating roughly 75% of export revenue. The government expanded Export Processing Zones to attract foreign investment, cementing the industry as the engine of Bangladesh's structural transformation.

title: BNP Wins Landslide Election; Khaleda Zia Returns as PM
description: The October 2001 general election, supervised by a caretaker government, gave the BNP-led four-party alliance 193 seats to the Awami League's 62, returning Khaleda Zia as prime minister for a second term. The peaceful transfer of power was widely noted as a consolidation of Bangladeshi democracy, though post-election political violence against minority communities was documented.

title: August 21 Grenade Attack on Awami League Rally
description: On 21 August 2004 a series of grenades were thrown at an Awami League political rally at Bangabandhu Avenue, Dhaka, killing 24 people and wounding over 300. Sheikh Hasina escaped with minor injuries. The attack — later attributed to Islamist militants with alleged state complicity — shocked the country and deepened political polarization.

title: Jama'atul Mujahideen Bangladesh Bomb Wave
description: On 17 August 2005 the militant group Jama'atul Mujahideen Bangladesh (JMB) detonated approximately 500 small bombs simultaneously in 63 of Bangladesh's 64 districts, killing two people and signaling the emergence of a homegrown Islamist insurgency. The government banned JMB and mounted a crackdown that led to the arrest and execution of its leadership by 2007.

title: Muhammad Yunus and Grameen Bank Awarded Nobel Peace Prize
description: The Norwegian Nobel Committee awarded the 2006 Nobel Peace Prize jointly to economist Muhammad Yunus and Grameen Bank for pioneering microcredit lending to the rural poor. With over seven million borrowers — 95% women — the bank model had become a global template for poverty alleviation and brought unprecedented international recognition to Bangladesh.

title: Military-Backed Caretaker Government Installed ('1/11')
description: On 11 January 2007 the military backed a state of emergency and installed economist Fakhruddin Ahmed as chief adviser after political violence made credible elections impossible. The caretaker government arrested both Khaleda Zia and Sheikh Hasina on corruption charges under a controversial 'minus-two' formula and remained in power until the December 2008 elections.

title: Cyclone Sidr Devastates the Southwest Coast
description: Category-5 equivalent Cyclone Sidr made landfall on 15 November 2007, killing at least 3,447 people and causing US$2.3 billion in damage. The Sundarbans mangrove belt absorbed much of the surge and saved lives, but the districts of Barguna, Bagerhat, and Pirojpur suffered severe destruction. The disaster prompted international debate on climate vulnerability.

title: Awami League Landslide and Return to Civilian Rule
description: The December 29 general election — the first in seven years — achieved an 80% turnout, the highest in Bangladeshi history. The Awami League and its Grand Alliance won 230 of 300 seats; Sheikh Hasina returned as prime minister in January 2009. International observers judged the poll largely free and fair, restoring civilian government after two years of emergency rule.

title: Bangladesh Rifles Mutiny and Pilkhana Massacre
description: On 25–26 February 2009 paramilitaries of the Bangladesh Rifles (BDR) mutinied at their Pilkhana headquarters in Dhaka, killing 57 army officers and 17 civilians in a 33-hour standoff. The massacre was the deadliest episode of intra-security violence in Bangladesh's post-independence history and triggered a sweeping restructuring of the paramilitary force, renamed the Border Guard Bangladesh.

title: Cyclone Aila Floods Coastal Districts
description: Cyclone Aila struck the southwestern coast on 25 May 2009, killing at least 339 people and leaving over one million homeless. Khulna district was worst affected; 9.3 million people across Bangladesh were impacted. Prolonged water-logging in coastal areas from breached embankments displaced communities for months, compounding damage from Sidr two years earlier.

title: International Crimes Tribunal Established for 1971 War Crimes
description: The Awami League government established the International Crimes Tribunal in March 2010 to try individuals accused of genocide and crimes against humanity during the 1971 Liberation War. Targeting primarily senior Jamaat-e-Islami leaders, the tribunal became a central and polarizing feature of Bangladeshi politics throughout the decade.

title: Fifteenth Amendment Abolishes Caretaker Government System
description: Parliament passed the Fifteenth Amendment in June 2011, abolishing the non-partisan caretaker government framework that had overseen elections since 1996. The Supreme Court had ruled the caretaker system unconstitutional. The BNP and opposition parties, which viewed the system as a safeguard against fraud, declared they would boycott any election held under a partisan government.

title: Tazreen Fashions Fire Kills 117 Garment Workers
description: On 24 November 2012 a fire gutted the Tazreen Fashions garment factory in Ashulia on the outskirts of Dhaka, killing at least 117 workers and injuring over 200. Locked exits prevented escape. The disaster — the deadliest factory fire in Bangladesh's history to that date — intensified global scrutiny of labour safety in the ready-made garment supply chain.

title: Shahbag Protests Demand Execution of War Criminals
description: Starting 5 February 2013, massive crowds gathered at Shahbag Square in Dhaka — eventually reaching hundreds of thousands — demanding capital punishment for Jamaat leader Abdul Quader Mollah, sentenced by the war crimes tribunal to life imprisonment. The movement spread nationwide and led to an amendment of the tribunal's law to allow appeals against lenient sentences.

title: Rana Plaza Building Collapse Kills 1,134
description: On 24 April 2013 the eight-storey Rana Plaza garment complex in Savar collapsed, killing 1,134 workers and injuring nearly 2,600 — the deadliest industrial accident in Bangladesh's history and among the worst globally. Structural cracks had been reported the day before but workers were ordered to return. The disaster galvanized the global fashion industry to establish the Bangladesh Accord on Fire and Building Safety.

title: Jamaat-e-Islami Registration Cancelled by High Court
description: On 1 August 2013 Bangladesh's High Court cancelled the registration of Jamaat-e-Islami, ruling that the party's constitution placed God above democratic processes in violation of the constitution. The decision effectively barred the country's largest Islamist party from contesting national elections.

title: Disputed Election Returns Hasina for Second Consecutive Term
description: The January 2014 general election was boycotted by the BNP-led opposition, resulting in 153 of 300 seats going uncontested and turnout of only 39%. The Awami League retained power, but the election's legitimacy was questioned by domestic critics and some international observers, deepening democratic backsliding.

title: Prolonged BNP Blockade and Political Violence
description: From January to March 2015 the BNP-led opposition mounted a prolonged blockade and series of hartals demanding a new election under a caretaker government. Petrol-bomb attacks on buses killed more than 100 civilians. The government's crackdown effectively dismantled BNP's street campaign but entrenched authoritarian governance patterns.

title: Holey Artisan Bakery Terrorist Attack in Dhaka
description: On 1 July 2016 militants affiliated with the Islamic State attacked the upscale Holey Artisan Bakery café in Dhaka's Gulshan district, taking hostages and killing 22 people — mostly foreign nationals including 7 Japanese, 7 Italians, and 3 Bangladeshis — before commandos ended the siege. It was the deadliest terrorist attack in Bangladesh's history and signaled a sharp escalation of jihadist violence.

title: Rohingya Mass Exodus into Cox's Bazar
description: Following a Myanmar military crackdown beginning 25 August 2017, approximately 655,000 Rohingya Muslims fled into Bangladesh within weeks — eventually exceeding 900,000 — making Kutupalong-Balukhali the world's largest refugee settlement. Bangladesh kept its borders open at enormous cost, hosting over one million refugees; repatriation talks with Myanmar made little progress through 2025.

title: Garment Sector Surpasses $28 Billion in Exports
description: Bangladesh's ready-made garment (RMG) industry crossed $28 billion in annual exports in fiscal year 2016–17, cementing the country's position as the world's second-largest garment exporter after China. The sector employed approximately 4 million workers, over 80% of them women, and accounted for more than 80% of total merchandise export earnings.

title: Awami League Wins Disputed 'Night-Before' Election
description: The December 2018 general election produced a near-total Awami League victory (96% of seats), but was marred by widespread reports that ballot boxes were stuffed the night before polling day, opposition candidates were obstructed, and observers were turned away from many centres. International election monitors noted serious irregularities; the BNP rejected the results.

title: Road Safety Protests and Student Movement
description: In late July and early August 2018, students across Dhaka and other cities mounted a major protest movement demanding road safety reforms after a bus killed two students at Shaheed Ramiz Uddin School. Tens of thousands of teenagers occupied roads checking driving licences. The government eventually made concessions on road safety legislation but cracked down on protesters.

title: Digital Security Act Enacted
description: The Digital Security Act (DSA) came into force in October 2018 and was used aggressively through 2019 and beyond to prosecute journalists, bloggers, and opposition activists for online speech. Human rights organisations documented hundreds of cases; several individuals died in custody. The law became the symbol of deteriorating press freedom under the Hasina government.

title: COVID-19 Pandemic Triggers Garment Export Collapse
description: Bangladesh recorded its first COVID-19 cases in March 2020. Global brands cancelled or withheld orders worth $3.18 billion in the RMG sector, forcing factory closures and lay-offs affecting millions of workers. The government announced a $500 million export-sector bailout; overall GDP growth fell to roughly 5% in FY2020, the sharpest deceleration in two decades.

title: Cyclone Amphan Causes $1.5 Billion in Damage
description: Super Cyclone Amphan crossed the Bangladesh-India border on 20 May 2020, killing at least 20 people in Bangladesh and causing an estimated US$1.5 billion in damage. The storm flooded coastal embankments and damaged crops in Khulna and Satkhira, compounding the economic stress of the COVID-19 pandemic.

title: Bangladesh Celebrates 50 Years of Independence
description: In March 2021 Bangladesh marked the golden jubilee of independence with state visits and international recognition of its socioeconomic transformation. The country had reduced its poverty rate from over 40% in the 1990s to below 20% and achieved gender parity in primary education, positioning itself as a development success story ahead of planned graduation from Least Developed Country status.

title: Protests Over Modi Visit Turn Deadly
description: When Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi visited Dhaka in March 2021 for independence jubilee ceremonies, Islamist groups led by Hefazat-e-Islam staged large protests against what they called Hindu nationalist symbolism. Security forces clashed with demonstrators; at least 17 people were killed, mostly in Chittagong and Brahmanbaria, in some of the worst political violence in years.

title: Padma Bridge Inaugurated
description: Prime Minister Hasina inaugurated the 6.15 km Padma multi-purpose road-rail bridge on 25 June 2022, the largest infrastructure project in Bangladesh's history at a cost of 30,193 crore taka (about $3 billion), financed entirely from domestic resources after the World Bank withdrew funding over corruption allegations. The bridge connects Dhaka to 21 southwestern districts and is projected to add 1.23% to annual GDP.

title: Foreign Exchange Reserve Crisis and IMF Bailout Talks
description: By late 2022 Bangladesh's foreign exchange reserves had fallen sharply — from over $46 billion in 2021 to below $34 billion — amid global commodity price inflation triggered by Russia's invasion of Ukraine. The government imposed import restrictions and rationed power, triggering rolling blackouts. Bangladesh applied to the IMF for a $4.7 billion loan package, marking its first recourse to emergency balance-of-payments support in decades.

title: IMF $4.7 Billion Loan Approved amid Macroeconomic Stress
description: The IMF's executive board approved a $4.7 billion extended credit facility for Bangladesh in January 2023, conditioned on fiscal reforms including broadening the tax base, improving monetary policy transmission, and strengthening the financial sector. The programme reflected the depth of the external-sector stress, with the taka having lost more than 25% against the dollar since 2021.

title: Student Quota Protests and Downfall of Sheikh Hasina
description: In July 2024 students mobilized against the Supreme Court's reinstatement of a civil service quota reserving 30% of government jobs for descendants of 1971 freedom fighters. Security forces killed hundreds of protesters during a violent crackdown. On 5 August 2024 Sheikh Hasina resigned and fled to India by helicopter, ending 15 consecutive years in power. Crowds stormed the parliament and her official residence.

title: Muhammad Yunus Heads Interim Government
description: On 8 August 2024 Nobel laureate Muhammad Yunus was sworn in as chief adviser of Bangladesh's interim government, taking office with a mandate from student protest leaders. The Awami League was effectively banned, arrest warrants were issued for Hasina and hundreds of party officials for deaths during the crackdown, and the government launched broad political and judicial reforms.

title: Rohingya Camp Violence and Security Deterioration
description: Throughout 2024–2025 the Rohingya camps in Cox's Bazar experienced escalating violence including murders attributed to the Arakan Rohingya Salvation Army (ARSA) and rival factions, with hundreds killed. Bangladesh intensified calls for international burden-sharing and raised the possibility of closing the camps if repatriation to Myanmar was not accelerated, as the camps' population approached 1.2 million.

title: Female Garment Workers Gain Economic Agency
description: By the mid-1990s approximately two million women were employed in Bangladesh's garment factories, the highest share of female industrial employment in South Asia. Studies documented measurable increases in women's education, delayed marriage, and household bargaining power. The phenomenon became a widely cited case of export-led gender empowerment in development economics.

title: Dhaka–Chittagong Highway Expansion
description: The Asian Development Bank co-financed expansion of the Dhaka–Chittagong corridor — Bangladesh's main economic artery linking the capital to its principal seaport — to four lanes. The project, substantially completed by 2003–2005, cut transit times, reduced logistics costs for garment exporters, and became a template for subsequent trunk-road investment under the ADB's transport programme.

title: Bangladesh Achieves Major MDG Gains in Child Mortality
description: Entering the 2000s Bangladesh had achieved a faster decline in under-five child mortality than most South Asian peers, halving the rate from approximately 150 per 1,000 live births in 1990 to under 80 by 2000. The gains were attributed to oral rehydration therapy, immunisation programmes, and expanded NGO health networks — marking Bangladesh's emergence as a development outlier.

title: Bangladesh Accord on Fire and Building Safety Signed
description: Following the Rana Plaza collapse, over 200 international brands and retailers signed the legally binding Bangladesh Accord on Fire and Building Safety in May 2013, committing to independent inspections of garment factories and remediation funding. The Accord covered over 1,600 factories by 2015 and represented the most significant industry-wide safety governance reform in Bangladeshi manufacturing history.

title: Dhaka Metro Rail Project Launched
description: Ground was broken on the Dhaka Mass Rapid Transit (MRT Line 6) project in June 2016, backed by Japan International Cooperation Agency (JICA) financing. Targeting one of the world's most congested cities, the metro was the largest urban infrastructure investment in Bangladesh's history and aimed to carry 60,000 passengers per hour, with the first section opening in December 2022.

title: Dhaka Metro Rail First Section Opens
description: The first section of the Dhaka Mass Rapid Transit Line 6 — from Uttara North to Agargaon — opened on 28 December 2022, making Bangladesh's capital one of the few megacities in South Asia with an operational metro system. The project was completed on schedule despite COVID-19 disruptions, signalling a step-change in Dhaka's urban transport infrastructure.

title: LDC Graduation Scheduled: Bangladesh to Exit Least Developed Country Status
description: Bangladesh is scheduled to formally graduate from Least Developed Country status in November 2026, following the UN Committee for Development Policy's recommendations in 2021 and 2024. Graduation reflects decades of sustained growth averaging ~6% annually and improvements in per capita income, human assets, and economic vulnerability. The transition will expose the RMG sector to higher MFN tariffs and is estimated to cost up to $8 billion annually in lost trade preferences.

title: Bangladesh Launches Its First Satellite, Bangabandhu-1
description: On 11-12 May 2018, Bangladesh launched Bangabandhu Satellite-1, its first geostationary communications satellite, aboard a SpaceX Falcon 9 Block 5 rocket from Kennedy Space Center. Built by Thales Alenia Space and named after independence leader Sheikh Mujibur Rahman, the satellite carries 40 Ku- and C-band transponders and made Bangladesh the 57th country to own a satellite.

title: Bangladesh Becomes First Country to Ban Thin Polythene Bags Nationwide
description: On 1 January 2002, Bangladesh became the first country in the world to legally ban production, sale, and use of thin polythene bags under 20 microns thick, starting in Dhaka before expanding nationwide. The ban was a direct response to bags clogging city drainage systems and worsening the catastrophic late-1990s Dhaka floods. Enforcement later weakened, but the law remains the pioneering global model for plastic bag bans.

title: Bengali Language Movement Martyrs Killed on Ekushey February
description: On 21 February 1952, Pakistani police killed student demonstrators in Dhaka who defied a public-gathering ban to protest the government's declaration of Urdu as Pakistan's sole official language and demand recognition of Bengali. At least five students, later honored as official Language Martyrs including Abul Barkat and Abdul Jabbar, died in the crackdown, and the date became Bangladesh's Shohid Dibosh (Martyrs' Day). The movement's linguistic and cultural significance led UNESCO to declare 21 February International Mother Language Day in 1999.
